name: 16x2 LCD (no I2C, 16 pins)
desc: Shows 2 lines of 16 characters with a backlight. This plain version needs 6 data wires plus a 10kΩ knob for contrast.
variantNote: Plain 16-pin version: more wires, needs a 10kΩ potentiometer for contrast.

warn.3.3: Standard 16x2 LCDs need 5V power. 3.3V signals usually work in write-only mode (RW tied to GND), but contrast can be weak.

name: 16x2 LCD with I2C backpack
desc: The same 16x2 screen with a small adapter soldered on the back, so it needs only 4 wires. Turn the blue screw to adjust contrast.
variantNote: I2C version: only 4 wires (VCC, GND, SDA, SCL). Address is usually 0x27 or 0x3F.

warn.3.3: The I2C LCD needs 5V, and its backpack pulls SDA/SCL up to 5V. With a 3.3V board, use a level shifter on SDA and SCL.

name: 20x4 LCD with I2C backpack
desc: A bigger text screen: 4 lines of 20 characters, still only 4 wires thanks to the I2C adapter.

warn.3.3: The I2C LCD needs 5V, and its backpack pulls SDA/SCL up to 5V. With a 3.3V board, use a level shifter on SDA and SCL.

name: 0.96" OLED 128x64 (SSD1306, I2C)
desc: A tiny, super-sharp screen that can draw text, shapes, animations and mini games. Only 4 wires.
note: Check the pin labels! Some boards are GND-VCC-SCL-SDA and others VCC-GND-SCL-SDA. Swapping power can kill it.

name: 0.91" OLED 128x32 (SSD1306, I2C)
desc: A slim strip-shaped OLED, great for a single line of big text or a status bar.
variantNote: SSD1306 chip, but only 32 pixels tall: code must use height 32.

name: 1.3" OLED 128x64 (SH1106, I2C)
desc: A bigger OLED that is easier to read. It uses a different chip (SH1106) than the 0.96" one, so it needs a different library.
variantNote: SH1106 chip: SSD1306 code shows garbage on it. Use the U8g2 library.
note: Check the pin labels: VCC and GND positions differ between sellers.

name: TM1637 4-Digit 7-Segment Display
desc: A bright 4-digit number display with a colon in the middle, perfect for clocks, timers and scoreboards. Only 2 data wires.

name: MAX7219 8x8 LED Matrix
desc: An 8x8 grid of red LEDs for pixel art, scrolling text and tiny games. Several modules can be chained into a long sign.

warn.3.3: The MAX7219 runs on 5V and officially wants 3.5V+ signals. 3.3V boards often work, but a level shifter makes it reliable.

name: 1.8" Color TFT 128x160 (ST7735, SPI)
desc: A small full-color screen for pictures, graphs and games. It talks over SPI, which is fast but uses 5–6 wires.

warn.5: The ST7735 signal pins are 3.3V. With a 5V Arduino, use a level shifter (many people add 1kΩ resistors in series instead, but that is a hack).

name: Single 7-Segment Digit (common cathode)
desc: One big digit made of 7 LED bars plus a dot. Great for dice and counters. Each segment needs its own resistor.
note: Common cathode: the shared pin goes to GND and a HIGH pin lights a segment. Use a 220Ω resistor on each segment.
